'''Itai Benjamini''' ({{Langx|he|איתי בנימין}}) is an Israeli mathematician who holds the Renee and Jay Weiss Chair in the Department of Mathematics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].{{r|www}} 

== Education ==
Benjamini completed his Ph.D. in 1992 at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], under the supervision of [[Benjamin Weiss]]. His dissertation was entitled "[[random walk|Random Walk]]s on Graphs and Manifolds".{{r|mg}} In 2004 he won the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] for young [[probability theory|probability theorists]] "for his work across probability, including the analytic and geometric, particularly in the study of random processes associated with graphs".{{r|nams}}
In the same year he also won the Morris L. Levinson Prize of the Weizmann Institute.{{r|levinson}}
He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010,{{r|icm}}
speaking about "random planar metrics".{{ran|B}} 

== Career ==
Benjamini was a long time collaborator of [[Oded Schramm]]. Their joint works included papers on limits of [[planar graph]]s,{{ran|BS}} noise sensitivity of [[Boolean function]]s{{ran|BKS1}} and [[first passage percolation]]{{ran|BKS2}}. With Olle Häggström, Benjamini edited the selected works of [[Oded Schramm]].{{ran|S}}

Benjamini has also made contributions to the study of the [[Biham–Middleton–Levine traffic model]] {{ran|AB}} and
[[isoperimetric inequality|isoperimetric inequalities]] on [[Riemannian manifold]]s{{ran|BC}}.
